selection.text: A dose–response curve shows how the magnitude and direction of a biological effect (the response) changes as the amount of a substance administered (the dose) varies. At intermediate doses the response often peaks because receptors become saturated or exhibit cooperative binding, giving a maximal effect, while at very low doses the effect may be submaximal due to a threshold for activation, and at very high doses the effect may diminish due to desensitization, antagonism, or tissue damage. Thus the curve’s peak can sit at an intermediate dose when the response rises to a maximum and then falls or plateaus as dose increases.
